title: AWS S3 Basics
summary: Learn how to plan and review an S3 bucket using the AWS console, without making changes automatically.

steps.title: Find Amazon S3
steps.instruction: Open the AWS Management Console using your own account and locate the S3 service. Do not share credentials or screenshots containing secrets.
steps.checkpoint: You can identify the S3 service home page.

steps.title: Choose a region
steps.instruction: Before creating anything, understand which AWS Region should hold your objects. Check your organization's requirements and data location needs.
steps.checkpoint: You can explain why the region matters.

steps.title: Review access settings
steps.instruction: Learn about Block Public Access and least-privilege permissions. For practice, keep public access blocked. Don't change live access policies solely on AI advice.
steps.checkpoint: You can distinguish public from private bucket access.

steps.title: Consider costs
steps.instruction: Review the applicable storage, requests, and data transfer pricing. Real AWS resources can incur charges. You may complete this lesson without creating a bucket.
steps.checkpoint: You know where to check pricing before provisioning.

steps.title: Review the workflow
steps.instruction: Summarize the region, security posture, naming constraints, and potential costs. If creating a real bucket, review every setting before submitting.
steps.checkpoint: You can describe the planned bucket configuration without exposing account details.
